diseases.name: Tomato_Early_Blight
diseases.description: Early blight is a common fungal disease affecting tomato plants. It causes dark spots with concentric rings on leaves, leading to yellowing and defoliation. The disease thrives in warm, humid conditions and can significantly reduce yield if left untreated.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Leaf drop starting from bottom of plant
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately. Apply copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil. Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation. Avoid overhead watering. Rotate crops annually. Use disease-resistant varieties. Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash.
diseases.prevention: Use disease-resistant varieties, practice crop rotation, avoid overhead watering, mulch around plants, maintain proper spacing, remove plant debris, and monitor regularly for early detection.

diseases.name: Tomato_Late_Blight
diseases.description: Late blight is a devastating disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. It causes water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, leading to rapid plant death. Can destroy entire crops within days in favorable conditions.
symptoms: White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb or chlorothalonil preventively. Remove infected plants immediately. Improve air circulation. Avoid working with wet plants. Use resistant varieties. Practice crop rotation. Destroy all infected plant material.
diseases.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, ensure good drainage, avoid overhead irrigation, monitor weather for favorable disease conditions, apply preventive fungicides, and remove volunteer plants.

diseases.name: Tomato_Healthy
diseases.description: Healthy tomato plant with no visible disease symptoms. The plant shows normal growth patterns with vibrant green leaves and strong stem structure.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular care and monitoring. Maintain proper watering, fertilization, and pest management practices.
diseases.prevention: Maintain good cultural practices, proper watering, fertilization, pest management, and regular monitoring for early disease detection.

diseases.name: Potato_Early_Blight
diseases.description: Early blight in potatoes is caused by Alternaria solani, affecting foliage and tubers. It reduces photosynthesis and can cause significant yield loss.
symptoms: Brown spots with target-like rings on leaves
Yellowing and wilting of lower leaves
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected foliage. Ensure proper plant nutrition. Improve air circulation. Harvest tubers when fully mature.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes, practice crop rotation, maintain adequate soil fertility, ensure proper spacing, and remove plant debris.

diseases.name: Potato_Late_Blight
diseases.description: Late blight affects potato plants causing dark lesions on leaves and tubers. The disease spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions and can cause significant yield loss. This is the same pathogen that caused the Irish potato famine.
diseases.treatment: Apply protective fungicides before symptoms appear. Remove infected foliage immediately. Ensure good drainage. Harvest tubers when fully mature. Store in cool, dry conditions. Destroy all infected plant material.
diseases.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid overhead irrigation, monitor weather for favorable disease conditions, use certified seed potatoes, and practice good sanitation.

diseases.name: Potato_Healthy
diseases.description: Healthy potato plant showing normal growth and development with no visible disease symptoms.
diseases.treatment: No treatment required. Continue regular maintenance and monitoring practices.
diseases.prevention: Follow good agricultural practices, proper watering, fertilization, and regular monitoring for early disease detection.

diseases.name: Corn_Common_Rust
diseases.description: Common rust is a fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi, affecting corn leaves. It reduces photosynthesis but is usually not economically damaging unless severe.
symptoms: Small, circular to elongate brown pustules on leaves
Premature leaf death in severe cases
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides if disease is severe and conditions favor development. Usually not economically damaging. Remove severely infected leaves if practical.
diseases.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, ensure proper plant spacing, practice crop rotation, and monitor weather conditions.

diseases.name: Corn_Gray_Leaf_Spot
diseases.description: Gray leaf spot is caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis, a serious corn disease that can cause significant yield loss in susceptible hybrids.
symptoms: Rectangular gray to tan lesions on leaves
diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides at early disease stages. Remove crop residue after harvest. Use resistant hybrids. Practice crop rotation.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant hybrids, practice crop rotation, manage crop residue, ensure proper plant spacing, and apply fungicides preventively if needed.

diseases.name: Corn_Healthy
diseases.description: Healthy corn plant with no disease symptoms, showing normal growth and development.
diseases.treatment: No treatment needed. Maintain regular care and monitoring practices.
diseases.prevention: Continue good management practices, proper fertilization, irrigation, and regular scouting for pests and diseases.
